frame / studio user manual

The app prepares photos of assembly steps at sizes given in millimetres and lays them out on an A4 cut-out sheet to print and cut. A 20 × 30 mm photo prints at exactly 20 × 30 mm.

  • No account or internet needed
  • Projects stay on the phone
  • Printed at 100% scale

First launch

The app opens with a splash screen showing the logo. On the very first launch four welcome pages briefly explain how to work with it.

  • Swipe or tap Next. Skip goes straight into the app.
  • On the last page the Tips on first use switch decides whether the app explains its screens. You can change it later in About.
  • Polski in the top right switches the app to Polish right away.
  • Get started closes the welcome screen. You can open it again from About.

In-app tips

The first time you open a screen, the app dims it and highlights its main elements one by one, each with a short description.

  • Next and Back move between elements, and the counter shows how many are left. Tapping the dimmed background also moves on.
  • Skip or the system back button closes the explanation. Each explanation appears only once.
  • The ? button is on every screen and replays its explanation. In the camera it sits in the top-right corner of the frame.

Hints at the right moment

Besides the explanations, the app reacts to what you do and gives a one-time hint in situations where mistakes are easy:

When it appearsWhat it suggests
The shot is 30 mm or smallerHow to approach a small detail, lock focus and when to use 2×.
Framing resolution drops below 300 DPIThat the print may look soft and how to fix it.
PN and steps share a cornerTo pick different corners in the Layout tab.
First visit to the Framing or Light tabHow to frame with your fingers and what the automatic correction does.
A project has at least two photosHow to save the PDF and print at 100% scale.
After the first PDF export with default printer settingsThat the test page helps you pick the brightening when prints come out too dark.

Projects

A project collects the photos of one assembly frame. The list shows all projects, newest first, with a cover made of the latest photos. Above the list the app greets you by time of day and reminds you how many projects you have and which is the latest; on first launch it invites you to create the first one.

  • New project asks for a name, e.g. the frame or station number. Create opens the empty project right away.
  • Tap a card to open the project. The cover shows the number of photos.
  • Top bar buttons: ? tips, printer print settings, PL / EN language, moon / sun light or dark theme. Your choice is saved on the phone.
  • Tapping the logo opens About with the version and this manual.

Project gallery

Tiles keep the proportions of the printed photos, so you can see at a glance which photo is narrow and which is wide.

  • Each tile has a sequence number (the same as on the cut-out sheet), the yellow steps label, and the size and PN number below.
  • Under the project name you see the number of photos and of A4 sheets they fill.
  • Tap a tile to open the editor. The photo smoothly grows into the print preview.
  • Add photo starts the three steps, and PDF saves the cut-out sheet.
  • ⋯ in the top right: Printer settings, Rename, Delete project. Deleting removes the photos from the phone, so the app asks you to confirm.

Adding a photo

The indicator in the top bar guides you through three steps: size, photo, details. The size of an existing photo cannot be changed, so measure the spot on the frame first.

  1. Size

    Enter the width and height of the spot in millimetres (comma or dot). The maximum is 190 × 269 mm, the printable A4 area.

    • The frame above the fields shows the proportion as you type.
    • ⇄ swaps width and height.
    • 20 × 30, 30 × 40, 50 × 70 pick the most common sizes.
    • Open camera turns on once both sizes are valid.

  2. Photo

    The white frame is the print area with the proportion from step 1. Only what is inside it gets printed.

    • Focus: tap a detail in the frame. The ring turns yellow and Focus locked appears. Focus and exposure stay set until you take the photo. ✕ on the bar releases the lock.
    • Zoom: 1× / 2× at the bottom of the frame, or spread your fingers. For small parts, zoom from a distance rather than moving closer than the lens can focus.
    • Grid splits the frame into thirds to help keep the frame straight. Flash helps in low light but causes glare on shiny parts.
    • The large round button takes the photo. The frame flashes briefly and a ring shows saving.

    Preview after taking the photo

    The preview shows the photo cropped to the size from step 1. Retake deletes the shot and returns to the camera. Use photo saves it to the project and moves on to the details.

  3. Details

    The editor opens on the Details tab. Both fields are optional, and an empty one does not appear on the photo.

    • PN number: exactly 10 digits. The 10/10 counter shows how many you entered. The photo shows just the digits, on a white background.
    • Steps: any text, e.g. S1, S2, on a yellow background.
    • Labels in the preview have the same physical size as in the PDF. On a narrow photo the text shrinks, but never below a legible minimum.

Photo editor

The top part is the print preview: exactly how the photo, with labels and printer settings, lands on the sheet. Below it are five tool tabs. Save keeps the changes. If you leave without saving, the app asks whether to discard them.

Framing

Spread your fingers on the preview to zoom in (up to 4×) and drag to move the framing. The Zoom slider does the same. The printed size does not change, and the yellow frame marks its edge. Framing resolution drops as you zoom; below 300 DPI a warning appears. Reset framing returns to the whole photo.

Layout

Four buttons per label pick its corner: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right. The white marker is the PN, the yellow one the steps. The label glides to its new corner in the preview. If both labels share a corner, a warning appears.

Light

Brightness and Contrast adjust this one photo. Automatic sets both to use the full tonal range of the visible framing. Reset restores the original values. Printer darkening is compensated separately, once for all photos, in the printer settings.

File

The print size and the photo's actual resolution at that size, including zoom. 300 DPI or more is enough for a sharp print. Delete photo removes the original from the phone after you confirm.

Printer

Most printers darken the midtones, and fine detail blurs on small prints. These settings apply to all photos: the preview in the app and the PDF export. Open them with the printer button on the project list, from the project ⋯ menu or from the Light tab.

  • Print brightening (0–40%): lifts the midtones and leaves white and black unchanged. The grey strip above the slider shows what the printer will be sent.
  • Sharpening (None, Light, Strong): computed at print resolution, so it works the same on a 20 mm and a 150 mm photo. Light is usually enough.
  • Black-and-white print: for laser printers. The app converts colours to greys with proper contrast instead of leaving it to the printer.

Matching the brightening to your printer

  1. Save the test page.

    In the printer settings tap Save PDF test page and choose where to save it.

  2. Print at 100% scale.

    On the target printer and paper, without fit to page.

  3. Pick a row.

    Find the row where the 80% and 90% patches are clearly different and the steps from light to dark look even. The current setting is marked ◀.

  4. Set the value.

    Set the Print brightening slider to that row's value. Below the rows you can also check the legibility of 4–7 pt text and 0.1–0.5 mm lines, and the header shows the print scale.

Cut-out PDF and printing

PDF in the project gallery lays out all photos as a cut-out sheet on A4 pages, at their exact sizes, and saves the file where you choose, e.g. in Downloads (the name ends with “_cutout”).

  • Header: project name, sheet number, number of photos and date. On the right, the Scale check: 50 mm ruler with millimetre ticks.
  • The scissors bar reminds you: print at 100% scale and cut along the dashed line.
  • Each piece has a dashed cut line exactly on the photo edge and corner marks (1–4 mm outside), handy for a guillotine. Pieces are spaced so neighbouring marks never mix.
  • The caption under each piece: the number in a disc (the same as in the gallery), the size and, if there is room, the PN number.
  • Print at 100% scale with “Fit to page” turned off. Before cutting, measure the ruler in the header; if it is not 50 mm, the printer changed the scale.

After your first PDF, if you have not changed the printer settings, the app suggests once how to pick the brightening with the test page.

Language

The whole app works in Polish and English. On first launch it follows the phone's language; after that your choice applies.

  • The PL / EN button in the project list's top bar switches the language instantly, without restarting. On the welcome screen use English / Polski.
  • The language covers every screen, tip and message, the saved file name, the cut-out PDF and the printer test page, and this manual inside the app.
  • Project names, PN numbers and steps stay exactly as you typed them.

About

Tap the logo on the project list.

  • The app version, with the build number in brackets, e.g. 0.8.0 (9).
  • User manual opens this manual in the app, also offline.
  • In-app tips turns explanations and hints on or off.
  • Show tips again makes every explanation appear again the next time you open each screen.
  • Welcome screen shows it once more.

Troubleshooting

The print is too dark

Print the test page from the printer settings and set the brightening from the row where the 80% and 90% patches can be told apart. For a single photo, use the Light tab.

The photo looks soft on paper

Check the resolution in the File or Framing tab; below 300 DPI, zoom out. In the camera, tap the detail to lock focus, and for very small shots step back and use 2×. In the printer settings turn on Light sharpening.

The printed size is wrong

Measure the 50 mm ruler in the cut-out sheet header. If it is shorter or longer, set the scale to 100% in the print dialog and turn off “Fit to page” or “Scale to paper”.

I want to change the size of an existing photo

The size is fixed because the photo was taken in that proportion. Delete the photo in the File tab and add a new one with the right size.

The PDF will not generate

The message says what is wrong. Usually a label is too long for a narrow photo; shorten the steps or increase the size. A photo larger than 190 × 269 mm does not fit on A4.

Labels cover an important detail

In the Layout tab move the PN or steps to another corner, or in the Framing tab move the photo so the detail is not in a corner.

Tips get in the way or have disappeared

In About turn off In-app tips or tap Show tips again. The ? button on every screen always works.

Where are my projects and how do I keep them safe?

Projects and photos are stored only in the app's storage on the phone. Uninstalling the app deletes them. Save the cut-out PDFs of finished projects to keep a copy.
